Nullable arrays

Source: R/io-values-nullable.R
io-nullable.Rd

Reads and writes the Elements nullable-integer, nullable-boolean and nullable-string-array (all version 0.1.0), groups holding values and a boolean mask.

Usage

write_nullable(store, key, value, kind, dataset_kwargs, path, call)

Arguments

store

An open rhdf5 file or group handle.

key

Name of the Element within store, "/" writes into the root.

value

The R value, with its records.

kind

The Encoding type to write.

dataset_kwargs

A list of dataset creation options.

path

Path of the Element within store.

call

The call reported by errors.

Details

R writes the nullable Element for the values Python writes it for:

  • an integer, logical or character vector with NA

  • a value read from a nullable Element, which keeps the anndata_nullable record (see dtype-records) so that it is written back as the same Element when it holds no NA

A plain character vector without NA is a string-array and a double vector is never nullable, because Python has no nullable float encoding. Integer values keep their On-disk dtype, so nullable-integer of int64 is read as double with an int64 record. The na-value attribute of nullable-string-array is "NaN" for new values and is restored from the record otherwise.

With the setting allow_write_nullable_strings set to FALSE, a character vector without NA is written as a string-array and one with NA raises anndata_nullable_strings_error, as Python raises a ValueError.
